jobs.objective: REVISE the RFC 0143 falsifiable implementation spec. Start from the design-v1 HOLDER.md (a required context doc); the design-v1 adjudicator returned needs_revision with seven findings F1-F7 (in SEED.md and the cycle-1 collaboration ledger context doc). Your revised HOLDER.md MUST resolve EVERY finding per its prescribed fix while RESOLVING THE FOUR OPEN QUESTIONS (which trust-model option 1-4 or combination; the surviving capability set + lifecycle of any new credential class; where the survival mechanism lives in source; and the legible-failure fallback) WITHOUT widening who can read the daemon's full-authority bootstrap admin client-token, and must not regress the parts the v1 ledger judged sound. Name the exact code sites (go/pkg/mutations/session_token.go, go/pkg/agentloop/token.go + endpoint.go, go/pkg/rpc auth prelude, go/pkg/admin/bootstrap.go, go/cmd/striatumd/main.go boot-epoch publish) and state every load-bearing security claim as a falsifiable assertion. This is the published claim the falsifiers re-attack.
jobs.title: Hold revised proposal

jobs.objective: Read the revised holder proposal and FIRST verify each design-v1 finding (F1-F7, in SEED.md and the cycle-1 ledger) is genuinely resolved in the revised spec, then write a falsifying challenge for RFC 0143 lane credential survival across a boot-epoch rotation, pressing hardest on the security/authz blast radius: any path that widens admin-token exposure, any durable lane-readable token file that can be replayed by a sibling process on the shared lane uid, any split-brain where a reseal token writes into a session the daemon has retired, and any Open Question or v1 finding 'resolved' without a concrete mechanism.
jobs.title: Falsifier 1 (security/authz lens)

jobs.objective: Read the revised holder proposal and FIRST verify each design-v1 finding (F1-F7, in SEED.md and the cycle-1 ledger) is genuinely resolved in the revised spec, then write a falsifying challenge for RFC 0143 lane credential survival across a boot-epoch rotation, pressing hardest on operator-ergonomics and lifecycle correctness: the OR-capability auth-prelude change, the lease-clock/heartbeat race, the per-adapter (Codex) survival matrix, the boot-epoch mirror integrity story, revocation/invalidation on session close, TTL bounds, file ownership/mode, and whether the legible-failure fallback truly makes the failure loud (self-escalating, routed) rather than swapping one silent exit for another.
jobs.title: Falsifier 2 (lifecycle/ergonomics lens)

jobs.objective: Read only the dialogue trajectory for the RFC 0143 revision (the revised HOLDER.md and the two FALSIFIER.md re-attacks) plus the SEED.md charter and the cycle-1 ledger context, and publish the collaboration ledger verdict (one of accept, accept_with_findings, needs_revision, reject — a clearing verdict is accept or accept_with_findings, never `clear`). A clearing verdict REQUIRES all seven design-v1 findings (F1-F7) resolved AND no new material challenge standing unrebutted AND the security invariant held (no admin-token widening, no replay, no split-brain). needs_revision if any of those fails.
jobs.title: Adjudicate dialogue substance

jobs.objective: Publish the cleared, falsification-hardened implementation spec (resolving all four Open Questions and all seven design-v1 findings F1-F7, with the chosen trust-model option and its exact mechanism) only after the adjudicator ledger records a clearing verdict; this SPEC is the artifact the rfc-0143-build run consumes. It MUST flag that the chosen option is a security/authz trust-model change requiring maintainer ratification before the build lands.
jobs.title: Commit falsification-cleared proposal

jobs.objective: Summarize the cleared collaboration gate and downstream publication.
